news.text: 6 November saw Players Software's budget action title *Joe Blade* vault to number one on the UK Gallup software charts across the **ZX Spectrum** and **Commodore 64**. Created by programmer Colin Swinbourne, the £1.99 infiltration platformer cast players as a lone military commando tasked with rescuing six kidnapped leaders held inside a complex terrorist headquarters. Featuring tight flick-screen exploration and a tricky sub-game to defuse explosive charges, the budget tape proved an irresistible staple in school satchels across the country.

news.text: 8 November saw tragedy strike Northern Ireland when a Provisional IRA bomb detonated near the war memorial in **Enniskillen**, County Fermanagh, during a Remembrance Sunday service. The explosion collapsed a gable wall onto the assembled crowd of civilians, killing eleven people—mostly pensioners—and injuring sixty-three others. The attack provoked near-universal revulsion across both Britain and the Republic of Ireland, severely damaging public sympathy for republican paramilitaries and galvanising British and Irish political leaders to seek fresh diplomatic paths toward peace.
news.youtube: Enniskillen Remembrance Day bombing 1987 news report

news.text: 15 November saw British pop-rock band **T'Pau** continue their iron grip on the UK singles chart as *China in Your Hand* held the number one spot during an imposing five-week residency. Fronted by fiery flame-haired vocalist Carol Decker, the dramatic power ballad took its inspiration from Mary Shelley's classic gothic novel *Frankenstein*, chronicling human hubris and delicate destruction. The track went on to become the 600th number one in the history of the British charts, with Decker's soaring vocal runs echoing out of car radios nationwide all winter.
news.youtube: TPau China in Your Hand official video 1987

news.text: 18 November saw a catastrophic disaster engulf the London Underground when a lethal fire erupted beneath a wooden escalator at **King's Cross St. Pancras** station, claiming thirty-one lives. Caused by a discarded lit match igniting accumulated grease and wooden debris, the blaze suddenly produced an explosive "trench effect" fireball that shot straight up into the crowded ticket hall. The resulting public inquiry under Desmond Fennell prompted sweeping safety overhauls, bringing an immediate ban on smoking across the network, the removal of wooden escalators and mandatory sprinkler installations.
news.youtube: Kings Cross fire 1987 ITN news report London Underground

news.text: 25 November saw John Hughes' beloved Thanksgiving road trip comedy *Planes, Trains and Automobiles* arrive in cinemas, establishing an enduring seasonal holiday classic. Pairing **Steve Martin** as high-strung corporate marketing executive Neal Page opposite **John Candy** as the garrulous, shower-curtain-ring salesman Del Griffith, the film charted their disastrous odyssey to reach Chicago through blizzards and burned-out rental cars. Audiences howled at Martin's profanity-laden car rental tirade before being thoroughly disarmed by the story's deeply touching emotional climax.

news.text: 26 November saw the WWF stage the inaugural **Survivor Series** pay-per-view in Richfield, Ohio, counter-programming Jim Crockett's NWA *Starrcade* on Thanksgiving night. The show introduced five-on-five team elimination bouts, headlined by a colossal main event that saw **André the Giant** lead his squad to victory over Hulk Hogan's team after the giant pinned Bam Bam Bigelow. Hogan subsequently stormed back out to brawl with his former ally, ensuring the burning feud between the two titans would roll straight toward *The Main Event* on prime-time television.
